site.title: Skool
site.short_description: Creator communities. Add a profile URL or link in public group posts when rules allow it.
site.long_description: Skool hosts paid and free groups. Owners set link rules. Public post pages often omit nofollow on outbound anchors in page HTML. Profile and social links usually use nofollow. Open the live URL and check rel before you treat a link as a ranking backlink.

opportunities.title: Profile bio link
opportunities.description: Add your site on your Skool profile. Profile and social outbound links use rel=nofollow on live pages. Use this path for clicks and brand, not pass-through DR.

steps.title: Sign in
steps.body: Open skool.com and sign in.

steps.title: Open profile
steps.body: Open your profile or account settings from the menu.

steps.title: Add your URL
steps.body: Paste your site into the website or bio field.

steps.title: Save
steps.body: Save and open your public profile. Confirm the link works.

opportunities.title: Group feed post
opportunities.description: Publish in a public Skool group when rules allow links. Public post permalinks often render body links without nofollow. Owners can remove promo. Confirm rel on your live post URL after publish.

steps.title: Connect Skool
steps.body: Install the OpenQuok extension, stay signed in on skool.com, and add the Skool channel.

steps.title: Pick the group
steps.body: Choose a public group that fits your topic. Read pinned rules for links.

steps.title: Write the post
steps.body: Add title, category label if required, and one URL in the body.

steps.title: Publish or schedule
steps.body: Publish with OpenQuok or schedule for your audience.

steps.title: Check rel
steps.body: Open the public post URL. Inspect your link in page HTML. If rel has nofollow, treat it as nofollow.

site.title: TinyLaunch
site.short_description: Startup launch platform with free Standard queue slots and paid Premium launches.
site.long_description: TinyLaunch lists startups with name, tagline, logo, and category. Makers create a startup profile, then schedule a free Monday Standard slot or pay for Premium placement. OpenQuok can autofill the create-startup form; you choose the queue and complete payment on TinyLaunch.

opportunities.title: Premium launch
opportunities.approval_time_hint: Usually within a few business days after you schedule
opportunities.description: Premium launch ($39 on tinylaunch.com/pricing) schedules your startup on TinyLaunch after you create the listing. Confirm link treatment on your live startup page after publish.

steps.title: Review pricing
steps.body: Compare Premium with the free Standard queue on https://www.tinylaunch.com/pricing.

steps.title: Create startup
steps.body: Sign in and complete the create-startup form at https://www.tinylaunch.com/dashboard/startups/new.

steps.title: Schedule Premium
steps.body: Pick a Premium slot and complete checkout. Confirm your live listing when TinyLaunch publishes it.

opportunities.title: Standard launch
opportunities.approval_time_hint: Free Monday slots; timing varies by queue volume
opportunities.description: Join the free Standard queue from tinylaunch.com/pricing, create your startup profile, then claim the next available Monday slot.

steps.title: Open pricing
steps.body: Review Standard (free) vs Premium on https://www.tinylaunch.com/pricing.

steps.title: Create startup
steps.body: Sign in and fill the shared create form at https://www.tinylaunch.com/dashboard/startups/new.

steps.title: Schedule Standard
steps.body: Reserve a free Monday slot when the queue allows. Open your live startup URL after publish.

site.title: Chrome Web Store
site.short_description: List a Chrome extension on the Web Store. Point Official URL, homepage, and privacy fields at your site to earn backlinks on the live listing page.
site.long_description: The store runs on google.com. Complete Store listing Additional fields and Privacy before you submit. After approval, open your public listing and confirm each outbound link.

opportunities.title: Official URL
opportunities.cost_note: One-time Chrome Web Store developer fee
opportunities.description: Set Additional fields → Official URL to your root domain (for example openquok.com). Check the link on the live store page after approval.

steps.title: Open Developer Dashboard
steps.body: Sign in at Chrome Web Store Dev Console and open your extension under Build.

steps.title: Set Official URL
steps.body: Under Additional fields, verify your domain if Google asks. Enter your site (for example openquok.com).

steps.title: Publish and verify
steps.body: Finish Store listing and Privacy, then submit. Open your public listing and confirm the official-site link.

opportunities.title: Homepage URL
opportunities.approval_time_hint: Same review as your extension package
opportunities.cost_note: One-time Chrome Web Store developer fee
opportunities.description: Homepage URL in Store listing → Additional fields links buyers to your site. Examples: browser extension landing or Chrome install guide.

steps.title: Open Store listing
steps.body: In the dashboard, go to Build → Store listing.

steps.title: Set Homepage URL
steps.body: In Additional fields, paste your landing or install page. Add Support URL if install docs live on another page.

steps.title: Check the live page
steps.body: After approval, open your listing on Chrome Web Store and confirm homepage and support links.

opportunities.title: Privacy policy URL
opportunities.approval_time_hint: Required when the extension uses user data
opportunities.description: Set Build → Privacy to your public policy URL. The store page can link out (for example privacy policy). Match the text to your declared permissions.

steps.title: Open Privacy
steps.body: In the dashboard, go to Build → Privacy.

steps.title: Add policy URL
steps.body: Paste your policy URL (for example privacy policy).

steps.title: Confirm on the listing
steps.body: After the listing is live, open the store page and confirm the privacy link works.

site.title: Microsoft Edge Add-ons
site.short_description: Publish an extension on Edge Add-ons through Partner Center. Set Website and Support contact on Properties. Set Privacy Policy URL on Privacy.
site.long_description: You submit extensions at Partner Center in the Edge workspace. Upload the zip package, then complete Availability, Properties, Privacy, Store listings, and Publish. Certification can take up to seven business days; there is no separate Edge Add-ons listing fee. See Edge extension install guide and Extension (Edge) for OpenQuok packaging. After the listing is in the store, open your page on Edge Add-ons and confirm each outbound link and rel.

opportunities.title: Website
opportunities.approval_time_hint: After certification, usually within seven business days
opportunities.description: On the Properties page, set Website to a page on your own domain (for example openquok.com). The URL must not point to your Add-ons listing. Users see this link on the live store page after certification.

steps.title: Open Partner Center
steps.body: Sign in at Partner Center. Open the Edge workspace and select your extension, or create a new extension and upload your zip package. See Microsoft Edge publish guide for the full flow.

steps.title: Open Properties
steps.body: On the left, click Properties. In Website, enter a page on your site (for example openquok.com or browser extension landing). Do not use your listing URL on Edge Add-ons.

steps.title: Publish and verify
steps.body: Click Save & Continue. Complete Privacy and Store listings, then click Publish on the Submit your extension page. When status is In the Store, open your listing and confirm the Website link.

opportunities.title: Support contact URL
opportunities.approval_time_hint: Same certification pass as your extension package
opportunities.description: On Properties, Support contact detail can be a support page URL or an email. Use a https URL on your domain for a backlink (for example Edge install guide). Registration values can also show on the store page.

steps.title: Open Properties
steps.body: In Partner Center, open your extension. On the left, click Properties.

steps.title: Set Support contact detail
steps.body: In Support contact detail, paste a support page URL (for example Edge install guide). You can use an email instead, but email does not give a backlink.

steps.title: Check the live listing
steps.body: Click Save & Continue and finish the remaining Partner Center sections. After certification, open your listing on Edge Add-ons and confirm the support link.

opportunities.title: Privacy policy URL
opportunities.approval_time_hint: Required when the extension collects user data
opportunities.description: On the Privacy page, set Privacy Policy URL to your public policy (for example privacy policy). The URL must work. Policy text must match the Data usage checkboxes and your extension behavior.

steps.title: Open Privacy
steps.body: In Partner Center, open your extension. On the left, click Privacy.

steps.title: Complete privacy sections
steps.body: Fill Single purpose, Permission justification, and Data usage. These fields must match your manifest and your policy.

steps.title: Set Privacy Policy URL
steps.body: In Privacy Policy URL, paste your policy (for example privacy policy). Click Save & Continue, finish Store listings, and Publish.

steps.title: Confirm on the listing
steps.body: After the extension is In the Store, open the listing page and confirm the privacy link loads.

site.title: Firefox Add-ons (AMO)
site.short_description: Publish a Firefox add-on on addons.mozilla.org (AMO). Set Homepage and Support site on the developer hub. Add links in About this extension. Add a privacy policy when you collect user data.
site.long_description: Submit a signed build through the Firefox Add-ons developer hub. AMO review can take days. Homepage and Support site appear under Add-on Links. You can also paste https links in About this extension — Mozilla routes them through outgoing and usually marks them nofollow. Check rel on the live page. OpenQuok ships a separate Gecko build; see Firefox extension install guide and Extension (Firefox) for build and ID wiring.

opportunities.title: Homepage
opportunities.description: On the AMO listing edit page, set Homepage to your site (for example openquok.com). It appears under Add-on Links on the public page. OpenQuok’s live listing links Homepage — verify rel on the rendered anchor.

steps.title: Open the developer hub
steps.body: Sign in to Firefox Add-ons. Open your add-on in the developer hub.

steps.title: Set Homepage
steps.body: In Edit, set Homepage (for example browser extension landing).

steps.title: Publish and verify
steps.body: Submit a new version or update metadata and wait for review. Open your public listing (for example OpenQuok on AMO) and confirm the Homepage link and rel.

opportunities.title: About description links
opportunities.approval_time_hint: Same AMO review as your add-on package
opportunities.description: The About this extension body on AMO supports rich text and markdown. Add https links to your site (for example Firefox install guide, browser extension landing, privacy policy). Mozilla wraps external URLs through outgoing and usually sets rel="nofollow" — verify on the live listing.

steps.title: Open listing edit
steps.body: In the AMO developer hub, open your add-on and go to Edit.

steps.title: Edit About this extension
steps.body: In the description or summary field, add markdown links or bare https URLs to pages on your domain (for example openquok.com and docs).

steps.title: Publish and verify rel
steps.body: Submit a new version or update metadata and wait for review. Open your public listing (for example OpenQuok on AMO). In About this extension, confirm each link href and rel.

opportunities.title: Support site
opportunities.approval_time_hint: Same AMO review as your add-on package
opportunities.description: Set Support site in the developer hub (for example Firefox install guide). Support email alone does not give a URL backlink. See Extension (Firefox) for self-host build notes.

steps.title: Open listing edit
steps.body: In the AMO developer hub, open your add-on and go to Edit.

steps.title: Set Support site
steps.body: Enter Support site (for example Firefox install guide).

steps.title: Check Add-on Links
steps.body: After approval, open the public AMO page. Under Add-on Links, confirm Support site href and rel.

opportunities.title: Privacy policy
opportunities.approval_time_hint: Required when the add-on collects user data
opportunities.description: AMO shows Read the privacy policy when you declare data collection. Host the policy on your site (for example privacy policy). Match the text to permission and data declarations in the add-on submission.

steps.title: Open privacy fields
steps.body: In the developer hub, open your add-on version or Edit. Open the privacy and data collection sections.

steps.title: Set policy URL
steps.body: Enter your policy URL (for example privacy policy) and complete data-collection disclosures.

steps.title: Confirm on AMO
steps.body: After approval, open the public listing. Confirm the privacy policy link under More information.

site.title: Fazier
site.short_description: Product launch and company pages for startups. OpenQuok fills the forms. You sign in and finish badges, comments, or payment on Fazier.
site.long_description: Fazier publishes launches and company pages. Launch pages link to your website. The free Basic plan asks for a Fazier badge or a link to Fazier on your site. Paid plans offer stronger backlink promises. See plans on https://fazier.com/submit. OpenQuok fills the forms. You approve and submit on Fazier.

opportunities.title: Page
opportunities.approval_time_hint: Usually within a few business days after you submit
opportunities.description: OpenQuok fills the company form at https://fazier.com/page/new. Add your name, website, and company story. Launch pages are the main path for links to your site. Check your live page after Fazier approves it.

steps.title: Sign in
steps.body: Open https://fazier.com and sign in with Google or email.

steps.title: Basic info
steps.body: Open https://fazier.com/page/new. In step 1, add company name, page address, website, logo, and tagline.

steps.title: Overview and socials
steps.body: Add industry, size, type, country, city, founded date, about text, and social links. Fill any extra fields Fazier shows.

steps.title: Publish and verify
steps.body: Submit the page. Open your live company page. Check any link to your website. Launches use separate rules on https://fazier.com/submit.

opportunities.title: Free product listing
opportunities.approval_time_hint: Basic tier: reviewed within about 30 days
opportunities.cost_note: Add a Fazier badge or a link to Fazier on your site.
opportunities.description: OpenQuok fills the product form at https://fazier.com/submit. Choose the free Basic plan. Add the badge or site link Fazier asks for. Launch pages usually link to your product site.

steps.title: Pick Basic (free)
steps.body: Compare tiers on https://fazier.com/launch, then open https://fazier.com/submit and choose Product launch and the Basic plan.

steps.title: Fill and review
steps.body: Use the OpenQuok extension to fill the form. Check each field before you submit on Fazier.

steps.title: Finish manual requirements
steps.body: Leave maker comments, add the Fazier embed badge or homepage/footer link, and wait for approval.

steps.title: Save your listing
steps.body: When Fazier publishes, open your launch page. Save the URL in OpenQuok.

opportunities.title: Paid product listing
opportunities.approval_time_hint: Lite Plan and higher can publish or schedule sooner
opportunities.cost_note: Lite about $29. Premium about $49. Super about $99. Fazier lists a different backlink promise for each tier.
opportunities.description: OpenQuok fills the product form at https://fazier.com/submit. Choose Lite, Premium, or Super. You do not need the free Basic badge or site link. Read each tier on Fazier before you pay.

steps.title: Pick a paid tier
steps.body: Compare Lite, Premium, and Super on https://fazier.com/launch, then open https://fazier.com/submit and choose Product launch with your paid plan.

steps.title: Fill and review
steps.body: Use the OpenQuok extension to fill the form. Check each field before you continue on Fazier.

steps.title: Checkout on Fazier
steps.body: Pay on Fazier. Paid plans do not need the free Basic badge or homepage link.

steps.title: Save your listing
steps.body: When Fazier publishes, open your launch page. Save the URL in OpenQuok. Check the link matches the tier you bought.

site.title: DevHunt
site.short_description: Launch platform for developer tools. Free listing with a permanent page, or a $49 launch week for a dofollow link. No badge required.
site.long_description: DevHunt lists APIs, SDKs, libraries, and other tools for developers. Sign in at https://devhunt.org/account/tools/new and complete the tool form. A free listing gives a permanent page with a nofollow link to your site. A paid launch week costs $49 on DevHunt and adds a dofollow link, homepage placement, and newsletter exposure. DevHunt removes listings that are not developer tools. OpenQuok autofills the form. You pick the listing or launch path and submit on DevHunt.

opportunities.title: Free listing
opportunities.approval_time_hint: Permanent tool page after DevHunt publishes
opportunities.cost_note: Free listing links use nofollow. No DevHunt badge is required on your site.
opportunities.description: List a developer tool on DevHunt at no cost. You get a permanent tool page with a nofollow link to your site. OpenQuok fills https://devhunt.org/account/tools/new after you sign in.

steps.title: Confirm developer focus
steps.body: Use this path only for developer tools. DevHunt removes consumer apps and general marketing tools.

steps.title: Read the launch guide
steps.body: Review listing vs launch rules on https://devhunt.org.

steps.title: Sign in
steps.body: Open https://devhunt.org/login and sign in with GitHub, Google, or email.

steps.title: Submit your tool
steps.body: Open https://devhunt.org/account/tools/new. Use OpenQuok to fill name, slogan, website, description, logo (about 220 by 220 pixels), and at least three screenshots. Put your product in the first screenshot. Submit the free listing on DevHunt.

steps.title: Verify after publish
steps.body: When DevHunt publishes your tool, open the live page. Confirm the website link works. Save the URL in OpenQuok.

opportunities.title: Paid launch
opportunities.approval_time_hint: You pick the launch week after $49 checkout on DevHunt
opportunities.cost_note: $49 one-time launch week on DevHunt: dofollow link, homepage spot, and newsletter slot.
opportunities.description: Pay $49 on DevHunt for a launch week. You choose the week and get a permanent dofollow link, homepage placement, and newsletter exposure. OpenQuok fills the form first. Checkout and launch week stay on DevHunt.

steps.title: Confirm developer focus
steps.body: Use this path only for developer tools. DevHunt removes consumer apps and general marketing tools.

steps.title: Compare listing and launch
steps.body: Read what the $49 launch includes vs a free listing on https://devhunt.org.

steps.title: Sign in and open the form
steps.body: Sign in at https://devhunt.org/login. Open https://devhunt.org/account/tools/new.

steps.title: Fill and submit
steps.body: Use OpenQuok to complete the tool form. Add logo (about 220 by 220 pixels) and at least three screenshots. Submit on DevHunt.

steps.title: Pay and pick launch week
steps.body: On DevHunt, pay $49 and pick your launch week. After publish, open your live tool page and confirm the dofollow website link. Save the URL in OpenQuok.
